provision_inventory.anchor: Section 4. No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce
provision_inventory.summary: Prohibits cities and towns from enacting, maintaining, or enforcing rent control of any kind, subject to narrow exceptions.
provision_inventory.reason: Preemption of municipal authority; does not impose limits on how much or how often rent may be increased.

provision_inventory.anchor: (a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption
provision_inventory.summary: Requires that property owner compliance with any municipal rent control regulation become entirely voluntary after six months.
provision_inventory.reason: Governs municipal rent control regulation terms; does not establish an in-scope rent increase limit.

provision_inventory.anchor: (b) such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy,
provision_inventory.summary: Bar on municipal rent regulation covering occupancy, evictions, units owned by owners with under 10 units, or units with fair market rent over $400.
provision_inventory.reason: Restrictions on municipal regulatory scope; does not establish statewide rent increase limits or just cause eviction standards.

provision_inventory.anchor: (c) a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners
provision_inventory.summary: Requires any municipality adopting rent control to compensate unit owners from municipal general funds for below-market rent differences.
provision_inventory.reason: Municipal compensation mandate; does not establish an in-scope housing rule.
